The speaker supported the Governor-General Amendment (Salary) Bill 2019, which raises the salary for the next Governor-General, David Hurley, from $425,000 to $495,000.

The Governor-General Amendment (Salary) Bill 2019 sets the annual salary for incoming Governor-General David Hurley in line with the Chief Justice of the High Court, with the salary fixed for his five-year term. The speaker praised Hurley's military and gubernatorial record and thanked outgoing Governor-General Sir Peter Cosgrove for his service.

The speaker supported the Governor-General Amendment (Salary) Bill 2019 to set the salary of incoming Governor-General David Hurley, but argued that the debate highlights the anachronism of constitutional monarchy and called for Australia to have its own head of state.

The Governor-General Amendment (Salary) Bill 2019 was supported on the Whitlam-era principle that the office should not depend on the holder's private wealth. Australia's constitutional monarchy was condemned as an outdated, elitist institution that excludes First Australians and non-British migrants and discriminates by gender and religion, citing George Nadel and Daniel Deniehy's 'bunyip aristocracy' gibe in arguing for an Australian head of state.
